references.text: Confession of sin as part of the atonement process, where Israelites are to confess the sins they have committed
Ezra confesses the people's sins and the sins of their ancestors, just as described in the Leviticus text
Nehemiah confesses the sins of the children of Israel, including his own sins and those of his father's house
The descendants of Israel confessed their sins and the wrongdoings of their fathers
The psalmist confesses to having sinned along with the fathers, done injustice, and acted wickedly
The accusation that the people have not obeyed the Lord's voice, parallel to walking in opposition against God
Confession of one's own evil and the wrongdoings of the ancestors, directly parallel to the Leviticus text
Daniel confesses sin and wrongdoing, both his own and that of his fathers, in prayer to the Lord
The promise that if we confess our sins, God is faithful and righteous so that He forgives us our sins
